clue.text: Strides a path to ruin

indicators.note: the letters are sent along a path that leads to their rearrangement, so the words before are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone strides along a track heading for destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'path to' signals that STRIDESA is rearranged; the leftover 'ruin' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a catastrophe, which is ruin in noun form.

clue.text: Took to horse as daughter tucked into a bit of fish

indicators.note: one piece is tucked inside another, so the daughter's letter sits within the fish piece

parts.note: roe is the egg mass of a fish, a small portion of it

explanation.surface: A rider mounts a horse while a daughter eats some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking to horse means mounting and riding, so the past tense of riding fits.

clue.text: This time around, first pull into pieces then throw cold water on

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the time abbreviation backwards before using it

parts.note: AD, anno domini, names the present era, this time

indicators.note: into puts the opening letter inside the chess pieces

parts.note: chessmen are pieces, so men

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Instructions to tear something apart and then pour cold water over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This time' is AD, anno domini, the present era; 'around' turns it, and 'first' takes the opening letter of pull, put 'into' chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen enthusiasm is to throw cold water on it, an idiom for discouraging.

clue.text: Lift consumes power — time to start a tedious walk

indicators.note: to start places the time letter at the front of the rest
consumes means one piece swallows the other, so power goes inside

parts.note: to lift something is to raise it
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: An elevator draws electricity, so it is time to begin a weary trudge on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumes' puts P inside RAISE for RAIPSE; 'to start' puts T in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A traipse is a long, wearisome trudge on foot.

clue.text: Old lag will do in a jam

parts.note: an old lag is a habitual prisoner, a con (convict)
something that will do serves the purpose, so serve

explanation.surface: A veteran convict will make do in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a jam' reads as trouble; 'jam' is the fruit preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A conserve is a fruit preserve, essentially a jam made with whole fruit.

clue.text: Vigil kept for a beetle

definitions.meaning: a watch kept over a dying or dead person
a wood-boring beetle whose ticking was taken as an omen of death

explanation.definitionFit: Both a watch at a deathbed and the furniture-boring beetle share this name.

clue.text: Measure adopted in face of rejection

indicators.note: a piece adopted in another is taken inside it

parts.note: the face of a clock or meter is its dial
an en is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A policy taken up despite being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: EN, a typographic unit, is a common crossword measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Denial is refusal or rejection of a claim or request.

clue.text: Playing around is a thing of the past

indicators.note: playing with letters means rearranging them freely

explanation.surface: Fooling around is something that people used to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinosaur is an extinct animal, and figuratively anything outdated.

clue.text: First man in right key

definitions.meaning: in cricket the opening batsman is the first to go in
a key that fits is something that opens a lock

explanation.definitionFit: An opening batter in cricket and a key that unlocks both go by this name.

clue.text: Reportedly tipped the scales for Virginia

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so we want a word that sounds like another

parts.note: to tip the scales at some amount is to have weighed it

explanation.surface: Someone apparently came in heavy on behalf of the American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virginia' is not the US state but the British tennis champion Virginia Wade, Wimbledon winner in 1977.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Wade is the British tennis player, so the surname completes her first name.

clue.text: Flower show out of place, shortage of air about

indicators.note: the show piece comes out of the place piece, set within it

parts.note: a point can be a place or spot
to set something out is to show or display it

indicators.note: about turns the shortened word round
a shortage of letters means the word is cut short at its end

explanation.surface: A floral exhibition is in the wrong venue and the air is stuffy.
explanation.walkthrough: SET goes into POINT for POINSETT; 'shortage of' cuts air to AI and 'about' turns it to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia is a Christmas plant prized for its red bracts, loosely a flower.

clue.text: Reach a time for volunteers at home

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Achieving a moment for unpaid helpers back at the house.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the British Army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain a goal is to reach it.

clue.text: Mistrustful head needs a replacement to be promising

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, is swapped for the letter a given here

parts.note: mistrustful means suspicious

explanation.surface: A distrustful boss must be replaced for things to look up.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening S of SUSPICIOUS is replaced by A.
explanation.definitionFit: Auspicious means showing good omens, so favourable or promising.

clue.text: Aunt Sally clips rough-spoken student smartly

indicators.note: clips means holds tightly round, so the target piece goes round the rest

parts.note: an Aunt Sally is a fairground target to throw at, a shy

indicators.note: spoken means we use the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: rough manners are rude
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A scold reprimands a coarse-mouthed pupil in a clever way.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British fairground game of throwing at a target; a coconut shy is similar. REWD, said, is rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewdly means astutely or cleverly, which is smartly.

clue.text: Danger lies in live model being cut near ribs

indicators.note: lies in means sits inside the other piece

parts.note: to live is to be
danger means risk
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so T can mean model

explanation.surface: A hazard surrounds a living model who is being operated on near the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like surgery, but it is a butcher's cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisket is a beef cut from the breast, just by the ribs.

clue.text: Catching great narrative, incorporating the same in Latin

indicators.note: incorporating means taking another piece inside

parts.note: an epic is a long heroic narrative
idem is Latin for the same

explanation.surface: Grabbing a grand saga that includes Latin repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic disease spreads widely, so it is contagious or catching.

clue.text: Don't care for real nut spread

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dislike for a genuine nut butter on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like a noun for toast, but it rearranges REALNUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being neutral means taking no side, not minding which way things go.

clue.text: Awfully tense in Lincoln? One wasn't there

indicators.note: in places the shuffled word inside the president

parts.note: Abe was Abraham Lincoln's nickname

indicators.note: awfully suggests a terrible jumble of the next word

explanation.surface: A nervous moment for the American president, but somebody stayed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges TENSE as SENTE, which goes 'in' ABE.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is one who is absent, someone who was not present.

clue.text: Gentle music or some big orchestra instead?

indicators.note: some means part of these words, so the letters run across them

explanation.surface: Should we have soft tunes, or would a large band be better?
explanation.definitionFit: Strains are passages of melody, especially soft or gentle tunes.

clue.text: Party worker to behave during lively visit? On the contrary

indicators.note: during would put the behaving piece inside the other
on the contrary flips the containment, so the visit goes inside the behaving piece

parts.note: to act is to behave

indicators.note: lively suggests the letters jump about

explanation.surface: A political campaigner should behave well on an energetic trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' alone would put the behaving inside the lively visit; 'On the contrary' flips that, so the shuffled visit goes inside instead.
explanation.definitionFit: An activist is a campaigner working actively for a political cause.

clue.text: Beheading, as regards improving future stock, could be giving the go-ahead

indicators.note: could be means the letters might form another word
beheading means removing the first letter

parts.note: eugenic describes efforts to improve hereditary stock

explanation.surface: A grim remark about executions as breeding policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beheading' takes E off EUGENIC; 'could be' rearranges UGENIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cueing an actor or performer signals them to begin, giving a go-ahead.

clue.text: Bidding with early start, he comes in on time an hour ahead

indicators.note: comes in means these letters enter the time abbreviation

parts.note: BST, British Summer Time, is an hour ahead of GMT

indicators.note: start takes only the first letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction issued early about someone arriving an hour before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' gives E from early; with HE that is EHE, which 'comes in' BST, British Summer Time.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is a command, someone's bidding.

clue.text: Blurred by embracing Shakespeare's very foolish, fond old man

indicators.note: embracing means holding the other piece inside

parts.words: Shakespeare's very foolish, fond old man
parts.note: King Lear calls himself 'a very foolish fond old man'

explanation.surface: Dim-sighted through hugging a doddering old king from the playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is Lear's own self-description in Act 4 of King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are dim and blurred, from tiredness or tears.

clue.text: Planned debate

definitions.meaning: to consider or discuss at length

explanation.definitionFit: Both intentional, as an adjective, and to weigh up, as a verb, share this spelling.

clue.text: Custom is for beginners to work on new tasks

indicators.note: beginners are the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: It is normal for novices to work on fresh assignments.
explanation.definitionFit: Wont means habit or custom, as in 'as is his wont'.

clue.text: Fleece left on court

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: to court is to woo

explanation.surface: A sheepskin left lying on a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleece is the coat of wool shorn from a sheep.

clue.text: Expecting young one to have nightmares

parts.note: an animal in cub is pregnant, expecting young
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman suffers bad dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi are demons once blamed for nightmares, and the word can mean the bad dreams themselves.

clue.text: Oarsman following managed to return thinner

indicators.note: following puts the oarsman after the other piece
to return means to go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to run something is to manage it, so ran
an oarsman is a rower

explanation.surface: A rower coming behind succeeded in getting back slimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrower means less wide, comparatively thinner.
